# Tomato — site digest

A functional 32-bit computer built from scratch in a dorm by Tyrone Marhguy, a Ghanaian computer engineering student at the University of Pennsylvania (Penn / UPenn), Penn Engineering Class of 2028. Full page index: https://tomato.tmarhguy.com/llms.txt

## What it is

Tomato includes a Dual-LUT ALU (`f(A,B,C) + g(A,B,C) + Cin`), a custom ISA (91 instructions plus NOP; 92 burned rows in a 512-row control ROM), Tomato OS written in assembly, a browser emulator that executes the shipped OS image, and Envelop for messaging the FPGA on the desk when a verified bridge holds a lease.

FPGA register file: 256 × 32-bit because there is no space for more. Discrete-faithful architecture count: 32,768 registers. FPGA CPU clock in the current Nexys build: 6.25 MHz (100 MHz ÷ 16).

This is chip-design work: RTL, verification, ISA, OS, and a discrete 74xx ALU slice. An ASIC implementation is a long-term goal. There is no tapeout yet.

## What exists today

- Tomato OS runs on FPGA (menus, games, video, input).
- Virtual Tomato runs the same OS in the browser.
- The discrete ALU board is fabricated and soldered; the rest of the discrete computer is still being built.
- ALU verification includes a recorded 130-billion-vector Verilator run plus formal checks at 1, 8, and 32 bits. Whole-CPU formal verification is not done.
